data.title: Iris forceps
data.summary: Forceps & clamps · Fine, narrow-bladed forceps with gradually tapering tips for delicate grafting work.
data.body:
![Iris forceps](instruments/iris-forceps.jpg)

_Also called: Fine forceps_

Fine, narrow-bladed forceps with gradually tapering tips for delicate grafting work.

## Parts
- Narrow blades tapering gradually (more gradual than Adson)
- Plain or fine-toothed tip
- Spring forceps - no lock or ratchet

## Types / variants
- Straight or curved
- Graefe, Stevens, Bishop-Harmon, Foerster, Gill, Tuebingen patterns (PPT1)
- Bishop-Harmon: fenestrated handle, fine tips (sometimes 1x2 teeth), horizontal or crisscross serrations (seminar)

## Uses / indications
- Miniature punch grafting
- Acne scar surgery
- Split-thickness and blister grafting (PPT1)

## How to hold
Hold like a pen with the first three fingers (between thumb and middle finger, index finger steadying); grasp dermis rather than epidermis to avoid crushing the wound edge.

## Sterilisation & care
Autoclave, hot air oven, 2% glutaraldehyde or boiling

## Viva points & tips
- Corrected from source: Khopkar/PPT2 mention a 'lock'; iris forceps have no lock
- Originally an ophthalmic forceps for handling the iris
- Bishop-Harmon is grouped here (PPT1 lists it as an iris forceps type; seminar gives a separate slide)
